help.content:
[b]Alpha15 options and anatomy[/b]
F10: MCP/VKLP permissions, tooltips, spoken language and installed voice, speech test, save/load settings profiles, export DNA. Connected bodies articulate; irises and pupils follow targets, with compound-eye alternatives. 88 paired loci encode fictional DNA; paid mitoses build/repair tissues and meiosis supplies haploid gametes. Mixed clonal/sexual strategies and cognition-dependent affect are possible. Profiles contain settings, not world saves.

[b]Alpha14 biology[/b]
Inheritance uses paired alleles with linkage, recombination and recessive load. Development spends reserves; adults produce finite egg/sperm reserves. Embryonic phases depend on energy, oxygen and temperature. Food particles refill gradually. Inspector shows developmental progress, gamete reserves and heterozygosity.

[b]Optional AI additions[/b]
MCP/VKLP are optional and do not change or disable normal controls. Connecting leaves live playback unchanged. Fixed stepping is explicitly selected. External knowledge may inform logged interventions; simulation observations can become evidence-backed VKLP claims. See docs/AI_INTERFACES_DE.md.

[font_size=26][b]GAN Organism Arena — alpha14[/b][/font_size]

[b]Starting world[/b]
New installations start in coastal habitat 7, with water, land and open sky. All founders begin in accessible water with aquatic respiration and weak terrestrial/flight capacities. Descendants can develop other capabilities through inheritance and mutation; they are not clamped to their ancestors' aquatic limits. An old default of habitat 5 migrates to 7 once. Other saved habitats and subsequent choices are preserved.

[b]Observe and control[/b]
Mouse: look. W/S: forward/back. A/D: strafe. Q/E: down/up. Shift: faster movement. Wheel: optical zoom. Shift+wheel: observer speed. L: a new random light direction on every press. This selects a fixed random sun angle; choose auto_sun in Settings to resume automatic movement. LMB selects, RMB follows behind the selected body's rear, Tab selects the next organism. Esc releases/captures the mouse.
F10: settings; F1: help. Both pause the simulation. Space: pause. 1–4: Natural, Cell, Neural, Energy views. 5: enclosed aquarium; 6: water/islands; 7: coast with sky; 8: land/shallows/air; 9: mixed water/land/sky. NumPad +/- changes world size. G injects an aquatic ancestor. F8 exports the selected body as OBJ. F12 saves a screenshot.
The water surface now has visible waves, highlights, stronger grazing-angle opacity, a visible underside and a shoreline contour. Waves are cosmetic around the mean simulated water level.

[b]Development and evolution[/b]
Individuals grow, mature, learn and age. Genetic evolution occurs across generations. Hatchlings, juveniles, subadults and adults have changing size/proportions. Suitable inherited combinations also permit an aquatic larva and, for small armored forms, a nonfeeding pupal stage followed by adult metamorphosis. Poor nutrition delays maturation. Each new offspring starts without its parents' learned hunting, flight or tool skills.
Skin, scales, feathers/quills, fur/bristles, mucus, membranes, horns, beaks and pigment patterns can combine. Coverings influence drying, respiration, insulation, drag, protection and energy cost. Feathers alone do not enable flight. Natural rendering is stylized instanced geometry; Cell view exposes schematic internal reproductive tissue as maturity develops.

[b]Reproduction[/b]
Compatible mature parents court and maintain contact for a fertilization phase. Egg-producing, sperm-producing and hermaphroditic roles exist. Genetic recognition/development differences, gamete roles and anatomy constrain crosses; a different family name or body plan is not automatically incompatible. All pairings do not necessarily produce viable or fertile offspring.
Aquatic external spawning, internal fertilization with egg laying, retention of yolk-fed eggs and maternally nourished live birth are distinct routes. Rooted photosynthetic forms use propagules and simplified gamete/pollen transfer. Clonal offspring require a separate inherited capability; finding no mate never grants automatic cloning. Reproductive tissue and secondary display traits mature with the body; they are not all modeled on mammalian anatomy.
Eggs or embryos take time and energy to develop. External eggs may dry out or be eaten; an internal brood depends on the carrier's survival. Developing offspring reserve population slots. Disabling new reproduction does not freeze existing embryos. Birth records both parents; parental-care traits can transfer real energy to nearby young. Times, anatomy, inheritance and fertility scores are simplified game rules, not a validated biological simulator.

[b]Habitat and survival[/b]
Respiration, moisture, body support and stamina constrain land and air transitions. Flight needs a suitable body, mature locomotion, practice and sky (7–9). Strong swimmers may breach briefly for low aerial prey; suitable land forms can snap at shallow swimmers or jump, and aerial predators may dive into shallow water. These moves spend energy/stamina, have cooldowns and use finite breath reserves. Bites require physical range and transfer actual prey energy.
Other possible combinations include amphibious life, pack pursuit/flanking, ambush, hiding, cleaning, parasitism, finite tools, upright gait, small insect-like forms, rooted filters, photosynthesis and land trees. No Earth species or evolutionary destination is guaranteed. Extinction is possible: automatic reseeding defaults off.

[b]Inspector and settings[/b]
Selection shows physiology, coverings, behavior, learned skills, life stage, reproductive route/progress, carried embryos, fertility and parent IDs. Global counts include developing embryos and losses. Settings control rendering, simulation speed/tick rate, mutation, population and visible-cell budgets, sound and thought text/Windows TTS. Visible cells and event history are bounded for performance. The current core is rule-based developmental artificial life, not a trained GAN or LLM controlling each organism.

[b]Files and installation[/b]
The portable installer reuses an official-checksum-valid nearby Godot ZIP and installs inside the project folder. No Internet is needed after setup. settings/config.json stores options; language/*.json stores translations; logs/ contains diagnostics; exports/obj/ and screenshots/ contain exports. MIT license: LICENSE.txt.

tooltips.language: Language of menus, status text and organism thoughts. Applied immediately.
tooltips.speech_language: Language used for spoken thoughts; follow uses the menu language. Requires an installed matching system voice.
tooltips.tts_voice: Choose an installed voice for the speech language. Automatic selects a matching voice; a missing voice never falls back to another language.
tooltips.mcp_enabled: Allow local AI clients to observe and control this world through the optional MCP adapter. Switching off rejects further access. Connecting does not reset the world.
tooltips.vklp_enabled: Allow the optional VKLP client to exchange world evidence and documented knowledge. Direct VKLP also works with MCP off. No automatic network requests.
tooltips.vklp_write_enabled: Additionally permit explicitly requested claim submissions to the configured VKLP ledger. Reading alone does not require this permission.
tooltips.vklp_url: Base URL of your VKLP service, for example http://127.0.0.1:8000. Remote services require HTTPS. Keep the API key in the VKLP_API_KEY environment variable.
tooltips.renderer: Graphics backend used after the next restart. Compatibility can help on older graphics hardware.
tooltips.auto_reseed: Automatically introduces founders if the world becomes empty. Off preserves extinction as an experiment outcome.
tooltips.fullscreen: Switch between fullscreen and a window without restarting the simulation.
tooltips.view_mode: Display natural tissues, separated cells, nervous tissue or energy colors. Biology and collisions use the same body in every view.
tooltips.light_mode: Direction of scene lighting. Automatic follows the sun; random chooses a new direction. The L key randomizes it directly.
tooltips.simulation_speed: How quickly simulated time passes compared with real time. Higher speeds increase the work per frame.
tooltips.simulation_tick_hz: Biological decision updates per simulated second. Higher values improve temporal detail and cost more CPU time.
tooltips.evolution_rate: Multiplier for within-life complexity and cognition development. Hereditary variation is controlled separately by mutation and crossing options.
tooltips.habitat_level: Choose habitat 5–9, from water to coast and sky. Changes available environments and abilities such as flight.
tooltips.world_step: Size increment used by NumPad plus/minus when resizing the world.
tooltips.organism_cap: Maximum living population plus reserved offspring slots. Lowering it prevents additional births until room is available.
tooltips.nutrient_count: Number of finite food particles in the world. Changing this rebuilds the nutrient field and changes food availability.
tooltips.visual_cell_cap: Maximum tissue cells per organism, plus at most one connecting segment per cell. Higher values show more anatomy and cost more rendering time.
tooltips.body_rebuild_interval: Seconds between checks for grown or changed anatomy. Joint animation continues between rebuilds.
tooltips.mutation_strength: Typical magnitude of inherited gene changes at reproduction. Stronger changes can help or harm viability.
tooltips.macro_mutation_rate: Probability of larger body-plan changes in offspring. Frequent large changes can produce poorly adapted forms.
tooltips.crossover_rate: Frequency of attempted sexual crossing, subject to maturity, compatibility and available gametes.
tooltips.viability_threshold: Minimum developmental stability required for reproduction. Low stability also reduces early survival.
tooltips.mate_cooldown: Recovery time in simulated seconds after reproduction before another attempt is possible.
tooltips.mating_radius: Distance within which a compatible partner can be found. Fertilization still requires physical contact or the appropriate spawning/pollination route.
tooltips.social_spacing: Preferred spacing in ordinary social movement. The body-contact solver separately prevents penetration.
tooltips.courtship_strength: How strongly compatible partners approach during courtship. Does not bypass biological compatibility.
tooltips.group_strength: Strength of cohesion and coordinated movement for organisms with social traits.
tooltips.predation_strength: Intensity of hunting and feeding interactions, still limited by anatomy, energy and available prey.
tooltips.hierarchy_strength: Influence of social rank on movement near other organisms.
tooltips.follow_distance: Distance behind the selected organism when following with the camera.
tooltips.follow_height: Height of the following camera above its target.
tooltips.camera_fov: Camera field of view in degrees. Smaller values zoom in; larger values show more surroundings.
tooltips.zoom_step: Change in field of view per mouse-wheel notch while looking around.
tooltips.audio_enabled: Master switch for environmental and organism sounds. Spoken thoughts have their own thought-mode setting.
tooltips.ambient_audio: Enable background habitat sounds when audio is enabled.
tooltips.organism_audio: Enable nonverbal calls of the organisms. This is separate from spoken thought narration.
tooltips.audio_volume: Volume of habitat sounds and nonverbal organism calls.
tooltips.organism_sound_interval: Minimum interval between sampled organism calls; longer intervals make the soundscape quieter.
tooltips.thought_mode: Off, on-screen text, spoken narration or both. The language stage of each organism determines its vocabulary.
tooltips.thought_interval: Seconds between displayed or spoken thoughts. Does not alter organism decision frequency.
tooltips.max_history_events: Maximum remembered events per organism used when composing thoughts. Older events are discarded first.
tooltips.save_settings: Save all current options as a named JSON profile. This saves settings, not organisms or world progress.
tooltips.load_settings: Choose a JSON settings profile. The complete file is validated before application; invalid files leave current settings unchanged.
tooltips.test_speech: Speak a short sample using the selected language and installed voice.
tooltips.rebuild_visuals: Immediately rebuild all organism anatomy and render resources from current genes and life stages.
tooltips.inject: Introduce a new aquatic founder into the current world, subject to the population limit.
tooltips.export_selected: Export the selected body as an OBJ mesh for inspection in a 3D application.
tooltips.reset_world: Replace the current population and world with a new simulation. Existing organisms and world progress are lost.
tooltips.close_settings: Close this panel and return to the simulation with the current settings.
tooltips.export_genome: Save paired fictional DNA chromosomes with mapped gene locations, complementary strands and genome metadata as JSON.
tooltips.contact_quality: 0–100: Lower values allow slight overlap and limit body contact correction passes. Below 90, ground support uses the centre of each body part; from 90, four footprint edges are also tested. 100 gives the highest accuracy at greater CPU cost. Default: 85. Applies immediately and is saved in settings profiles. The number is a quality level, not an accuracy percentage.
